correctness.rationale: The proof reconstructs the character group of the (Z/n)^5 complete-quadrangle cover, applies the standard eigensheaf formula L_a=dL-sum b_v E_v, and computes every h^1 on Bl_4(P2). Riemann--Roch and Serre duality reduce possible contributions to (d,k)=(2,1) and (4,4); elementary K4 identities exclude all other cases. The two surviving character families have cardinalities 4*C(n-1,2) and C(n-1,2), respectively. The p_g and local-cohomology statements then follow from the cited chi formula and the standard section-ring correspondence. The finite replay independently reproduces the counts for n=2 through 8 but is not used as proof for arbitrary n.

The closest older same-object paper by Bauer--Catanese gives rigidity and explicit equations for the complete-quadrangle Hirzebruch-Kummer covers, but targeted text and exact-formula searches did not locate the formula q=5*C(n-1,2). The accepted statement is therefore a statement-level strengthening rather than a restatement of positivity. Search failure is not treated as a proof of novelty; classical complete-quadrangle literature is retained as a residual risk.

value.rationale: Irregularity is a basic intrinsic Hodge invariant of the classical second Hirzebruch family, and Anghel's recent application explicitly needs only a witness that it is nonzero. The exact formula classifies the entire H^1 contribution across an infinite family, yields p_g exactly from the already-known chi, and quantifies the degree-zero Cohen--Macaulay defect of the new quasi-Gorenstein section rings that have no graded maximal Cohen--Macaulay modules. This is a natural structural completion of a highlighted gap rather than an arbitrary numerical slice.
